newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine roadblock protestors set job demands.
newsitem.headline: Argentine roadblock protestors set job demands.

text.p: Thousands of northeastern Argentine protestors who have blocked roads to Bolivia for five days finally agreed among themselves Monday on their conditions for lifting their road barriers.

Their seven-page list of demands, all concerning government job creation measures, was hammered out after a long assembly and approved by 15,000 protestors after a debate which lasted much of the night, the state-owned Telam news agency reported.
Telam did not give details of the demands.

The demonstrators from the impoverished towns of Tartagal, General Mosconi and Aguaray near the Bolivian border in the northwestern province of Salta are also blocking traffic going 220 miles (350 km) south to the city of Salta.
The Clarin newspaper reported that 30 trucks loaded with goods for export to Bolivia were stuck behind the barricades of car tires and wood piled on national route 34 Sunday.

Argentina's national unemployment rate is 17.3 percent, but poverty is much more acute in provinces like Salta. The area of Tartagal has suffered from job cuts by former state oil firm YPF and over 50 percent of the local workforce is unemployed.
Talks with the provincial government broke down Saturday after the demonstrators rejected an offer to create 2,000 jobs in the zone, but officials hoped to reestablish contact soon.

"Solutions need time. There are no instant solutions, so it's important to get the dialogue going again and stop the roadblock, so that we can try to find definitive solutions together," Salta Deputy Governor Walter Wayar said.
He said he hoped the national governent would assist Salta in creating jobs.
The demonstration has generally been peaceful, but protestors annoyed at media coverage of the events commandeered a truck carrying the local El Tribuno newspaper and burnt 6,000 copies Saturday,
